data.name: Hrutik
data.gender_notes: Hrutik is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root hruth, which means protection, the name Hrutik denotes one who protects, guards or safeguards. In Hindu mythology, Hrutik is the name of a deity who is believed to protect the heart, guarding it against negative emotions and malevolent influences. The name Hrutik carries the meaning “He who protects” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hrutik usually hope their child will grow to embody he who protects and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Hrutik belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “He who protects.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hrutik total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name Hrutik signifies a deep connection to the divine guardian who ensures the safety of one's heart. Shri Hrutik Deva, a protective deity, is believed to provide emotional well-being and protection from inner turmoil and negative thoughts. historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, mentions a king named Hrutik, who was a contemporary of the Pandava prince Bhima. Hrutik was a king of the Vaisya (merchant) community in the kingdom of Khandava. Bhima once visited Hrutik's kingdom and was impressed by his wealth and hospitality.

The Puranas, a set of ancient Hindu texts, describe Hrutik as a king of the Haihayas, a Yadava (Jain) dynasty. Hrutik is said to have ruled over the region of Mathura in present-day Uttar Pradesh, India. According to the texts, Hrutik was a just and wise ruler who was revered by his subjects.
